options.content:
### Severe weather reports — NOAA / National Weather Service

The *Local Storm Reports* that the 122 forecast offices of the NWS publish every day, aggregated by
Esri into a public Feature Service and read live: the dashboard began as a replica of
[Esri's ArcGIS dashboard](https://www.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/94054353efa943b781cc5d6176ca8283) on the same data.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Source** | `NOAA_storm_reports_v1/FeatureServer/4` — *ALL Storm Reports (past week)*, no token |
| **Pipeline** | one request from your browser (`f=json`) → DuckDB-WASM (Chaski) → every panel, with Mosaic for the linked views |
| **Coverage** | rolling 7-day window, up to 10,000 reports, read when you open the dashboard (the service updates every 15 minutes: reload the page for the newest) |
| **Licence** | public domain (NOAA); service hosted by Esri |

**Everything is answered in your browser.** The timeline, the filters, the map and the cards share one
Mosaic selection: drag a brush, pick a type or a state, press play, draw an area or pan the map, and
the rest follows as you move, with no request to the service. The cards and the table count what is in
the map's view. `MAGNITUDE` mixes units by type (hail in inches, gusts in mph, snow in inches, tornado
EF numbers), so it is in the tooltip, the table and the cards of its own type, and drives no point size.
The *hour of day* is local solar time, from each report's longitude, so an afternoon storm in
Florida and one in Arizona fall at the same hour whatever their time zones.

spec.rawSql:
-- The whole week, once: time, type, state, hour and source are filtered in the map, on the GPU,
-- where the clauses of the stormFilters Mosaic selection land.
SELECT id, time, latitude, longitude, type, type_group, location, county, state, mag, measurement, source, office, deaths, injuries, casualties, solar_hour, comment
FROM $reports

SELECT id, time, latitude, longitude, type, type_group, location, county, state, mag, measurement, source, office, deaths, injuries, casualties, solar_hour, comment
FROM $reports
WHERE casualties > 0

spec.description: Every report of the week, coloured by type, with density hexbins and the reports that cost lives or injuries ringed in white. Filtered in the map by the timeline and the filters; draw an area to filter every other panel. Pan or zoom and the counts follow what is on screen.
spec.title: Severe weather reports — last 7 days

spec.rawSql:
SELECT time, type, location, state, mag, comment, latitude, longitude
FROM $reports
WHERE $__crossfilter($stormFilters)
  -- The map's view, which reaches Mosaic as a live clause and this table as its four edges.
  AND longitude BETWEEN coalesce(try_cast($west AS DOUBLE), -180) AND coalesce(try_cast($east AS DOUBLE), 180)
  AND latitude BETWEEN coalesce(try_cast($south AS DOUBLE), -90) AND coalesce(try_cast($north AS DOUBLE), 90)
ORDER BY time DESC
LIMIT 200

source.sql:
-- The week of Local Storm Reports, read once by your browser from NOAA's public
-- ArcGIS service (it allows any origin) and kept in DuckDB-WASM: every panel below
-- answers from here, with no further request to the service.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT unnest(f.attributes)
  FROM read_json('https://services9.arcgis.com/RHVPKKiFTONKtxq3/arcgis/rest/services/NOAA_storm_reports_v1/FeatureServer/4/query?where=INCIDENT_DATETIME%20IS%20NOT%20NULL&outFields=OBJECTID,INCIDENT_DATETIME,INCIDENT_TYPE,MAGNITUDE,MEASUREMENT,LOCATION,COUNTY,STATE,LATITUDE,LONGITUDE,SOURCE,OFFICE,FATALITIES,INJURIES,COMMENTS&orderByFields=OBJECTID&returnGeometry=false&maxRecordCountFactor=10&resultRecordCount=10000&f=json'), unnest(features) AS t(f)
)
SELECT
  OBJECTID::BIGINT AS id,
  to_timestamp(INCIDENT_DATETIME / 1000) AS time,
  INCIDENT_TYPE::VARCHAR AS type,
  -- The map's and the chart's colours: the nine types they name, the rest as Other.
  CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE IN ('Tornado', 'Hail', 'Wind Gust', 'Wind Damage', 'Flash Flood', 'Flood', 'Snow', 'Lightning', 'Wildfire') THEN INCIDENT_TYPE ELSE 'Other' END AS type_group,
  MAGNITUDE::DOUBLE AS mag,
  MEASUREMENT::VARCHAR AS measurement,
  LOCATION::VARCHAR AS location,
  COUNTY::VARCHAR AS county,
  STATE::VARCHAR AS state,
  LATITUDE::DOUBLE AS latitude,
  LONGITUDE::DOUBLE AS longitude,
  SOURCE::VARCHAR AS source,
  OFFICE::VARCHAR AS office,
  coalesce(FATALITIES, 0)::INTEGER AS deaths,
  coalesce(INJURIES, 0)::INTEGER AS injuries,
  (coalesce(FATALITIES, 0) + coalesce(INJURIES, 0))::INTEGER AS casualties,
  -- Local solar time, from the longitude (15 degrees an hour): the sun's clock at
  -- the report, the same for every state whatever its time zone or daylight saving.
  round(((INCIDENT_DATETIME / 3600000.0 + LONGITUDE / 15) % 24 + 24) % 24, 2) AS solar_hour,
  COMMENTS::VARCHAR AS comment
FROM r
WHERE LATITUDE IS NOT NULL AND LONGITUDE IS NOT NULL
